messages:
ana: Quick sync — post-launch triage. Two customer-facing regressions + a UX polish ask. Need to decide hotfix vs next-sprint work.

liam: Can you paste issue links / repros? Are regressing endpoints P1?

ana: TL;DR:
- REG-A: embeddings truncated on >65k input, affects OCR pipeline for 3 customers (P1)
- REG-B: websocket stream drops after ~512 tokens, intermittent, lower volume (P2)
- ENH-1: autocomplete suggestions are noisy on long prompts (UX polish)

ana: repro snippet (REG-A):
```bash
curl -X POST /v1/embeddings -d '{"input": "<big_document>"}'
# returns shorter vector length than baseline
```

sophia: If REG-A is P1 we should push a targeted patch — likely revert the new chunked-kv cache heuristic. @eng-runtime :thumbsup:

jen: I can own the revert PR and smoke tests. ETA ~4h if no blocker.

mike: Tradeoffs? Reverting will increase token latency and reduce throughput ~8-12% for peak traffic for 24-48h.

liam: Is there a smaller fix? Maybe guardrail for big inputs (reject+400 with helpful message) until we ship the revert?

sophia: Guardrail buys time for canary fix; but customer impact is higher (they can't process large docs). For 3 paying customers P1, revert seems ok.

ana: Decision leaning revert + canary to prod next 6h. Actions:
- jen: open PR + merge to hotfix branch (owner)
- eng-runtime: monitor latency/throughput dashboard, rollback if >15% perf hit
- release-bot: schedule hotfix deploy to canary 01 (non-prod) then prod canary

release-bot: deploy scheduled to canary-01 at 5155551300 by jen-bot

jen: PR #482 opened -> targeting canary after tests. I'll post status here.

mike: For backlog — ENH-1 will go into next sprint; assign to UX lane. Let's also run a 30-min grooming to re-evaluate priority vs other polish asks.

ana: Grooming meeting booked: tomorrow 10:00AM PT. Agenda: scope, owners, acceptance criteria.

liam: Thanks all. Will update the customer success leads and set expectation (ETA for full fix 5 working days).

sophia: :thumbsup:
